# National Funeral Directors Association

National Funeral Directors Association is a nonprofit organization. National Funeral Director's Association is an organization that provides education, certifications, training, continuing education calendar, on-demand learning, international professional achievement certificate, national emerging leaders program, licensing boards and reqs, and ce approval requirements. National Funeral Directors Association employs 57 people and has an annual revenue of $4.5M, founded in 1882. Headquartered in Brookfield, Wisconsin, United States, with an office in Seal Beach. Its workforce is distributed across 6 countries (including United States, Singapore, Brazil, Bahamas, and United Kingdom).

## About

NFDA is the world’s leading and largest funeral service association, serving 18,500 individual members who represent nearly 10,000 funeral homes in the United States and 43 countries around the world. NFDA is the trusted leader, beacon for ethics and the strongest advocate for the profession. NFDA is the association of choice because it offers funeral professionals comprehensive educational resources, tools to manage successful businesses, guidance to become pillars in their communities and the expertise to foster future generations of funeral professionals. NFDA is headquartered in Brookfield, Wis., and has an office in Washington, D.C. For more information, visit www.nfda.org.

Community Need

# Illinois Funeral Directors Association

Illinois Funeral Directors Association is a nonprofit organization. The Illinois Funeral Directors Association (ifda) is an association founded in 1881 by funeral directors seeking a common voice. They provide membership benefits, career center opportunities, and job search services for funeral directors, owning funeral homes, and with funeral service related businesses. Illinois Funeral Directors Association employs 2 people and has an annual revenue of $11M, founded in 1881. Headquartered in Springfield, Illinois, United States.

## About

On December 14, 1881, the Illinois Undertakers Association met and elected its first corps of officers. Led by new president Joseph Rogerson (Chicago), they intended to "organize a state association to which undertakers might belong," according to The Casket (January, 1882), and to "take such action, after its organization as a state society, as it might deem proper for the protection of its members and the business." Another important goal was to "secure state legislation providing for the licensing of undertakers - and to provide that none shall be licensed as undertakers but such as may be duly qualified to perform the many delicate offices of a modern undertaker, one of the most important of which is the embalming of bodies." Annual meetings have been held nearly every year since.
 
Today, the Illinois Funeral Directors Association represents 650 funeral home and 1,300 funeral director and embalmer members seeking a common voice, a way to share information, ideas, and methods, and to protect themselves and consumers through legislation. We offer a variety of services to our members and to the general public. We invite you to review the information on this website and contact us with any question you may have.

# American Computer Development, Inc. (ACDi) "​In Touch With Technology"​ (American Computer Development, Inc.)

American Computer Development, Inc. (ACDi) "​In Touch With Technology"​ is a Appliances, Electrical, and Electronics Manufacturing company. ACDi is a leading U.S. Based electronics manufacturer and PCB design company providing flexible manufacturing, and high-quality product life-cycle management. American Computer Development, Inc. (ACDi) "​In Touch With Technology"​ employs 71 people (+2.3% YoY, +3 people) and has an annual revenue of $690.2K, founded in 1984.
